messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 2-iodopyridine with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:

Experiments so far (best first):

Propose exactly 5 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"ligand": "<label>", "base": "<label>", "additive": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: A3 gives the best observed yield with L1, and testing the untried B3 checks whether the strong result can improve with a different base.
A3 substantially outperforms other tested additives with L2, while B1 may improve on the observed L2/B2 result.
This tests whether the untried B3 can rescue L2 while retaining the best-performing additive.
The poor L3 result used A16, so pairing L3 with the standout A3 isolates whether the ligand can perform well in the favored additive regime.
The prior L4 result used A21, and testing A3 with the same base checks whether the strong additive can substantially improve its performance.
